I've farmed this land since I was young. My mother grew wheat and corn, and her mother before her. In Quzhou, everyone around here grows winter wheat then summer corn on the same fields — that's just what our land is for. I have about 8 mu. My husband helps when he can, but his back is bad, so mostly it's me and my neighbor's son with the machine.

I'll plant wheat this October the same way I always have. I get the improved seed from the village seed shop — not the very expensive hybrid kind, but the good improved variety they've been pushing for years, gives me decent yield. I put down compound fertilizer when I sow, then spread urea at jointing and again before heading. I water three times: once in November before the ground freezes (that's the most important one), once when the wheat joints, once when it heads. I spray for weeds in early spring and once for rust before harvest — rust was bad two years ago and I lost a lot that year, so I don't skip it now.

After I harvest the wheat in June, I rotary-till right away and get the corn in the ground fast — can't waste days. Corn I use hybrid seed, always have for corn, everyone does, the yield difference is obvious. I fertilize corn twice — compound at planting, urea when it's about knee-high. If July is dry I'll water once at the big bell stage, but most years the summer rains take care of it. I spray once for stem borer if I see the damage starting.
